statement: For every 99-by-99 symmetric binary zero-diagonal matrix A with exact integer row degree14, put r_uv=(A^2)_uv+A_uv-2 for u<v, F3=sum_[u<v] 1[3 does not divide r_uv] and E=sum_[u<v] r_uv^2. Then F3<=E<=28*F3. If q_i counts these unordered residuals congruent to i modulo3, q1-q2 is divisible by3; the same congruence holds in every complete vertex row. Consequently F3=1 is impossible and F3=2 implies q1=q2=1. No existence or realization of these small defects is asserted.

independent_path: Count middle vertices: sum_[u<v] CN_uv=99*binom(14,2)=9009, with693 edges and4851 pairs, so the residual sum is zero.
At edges CN<=13 and at nonedges CN<=14, so -2<=r<=12.
Positive residual mass P equals absolute negative mass N; E<=12P+2N=14N and N<=2F3.
Each residue violation has nonzero integer residual and contributes at least1 to E.
Each complete row has residual sum182+14-196=0; reduction modulo3 proves both histogram congruences and the F3=1/2 consequences.
